chunks: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
If a man purchases a bondwoman while she has not yet reached maturity, or she has despaired of menstruation, then there is no harm in his not observing istibrāʾ for her.

key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a bondwoman or female slave who is purchased
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.يَئِسَتْ مِنَ الْحَيْضِ: has passed the age of menstruation
key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَهَا: to observe istibrāʾ for her, meaning a waiting period to ensure absence of pregnancy

ai.seo_question: When is istibrāʾ not required for a purchased bondwoman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning istibrāʾ for a purchased bondwoman. It states that if she has not yet reached maturity or has passed the age of menstruation, there is no harm in not observing the waiting period intended to ensure absence of pregnancy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4546 - Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"If a man purchases a bondwoman who has not yet reached maturity or has passed the age of menstruation, then there is no harm if he does not observe an istibra' (waiting period) for her."
